q6.answer: Order drives the flow. Its orders table holds the current status (PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED and so on), and order_status_history records each step a checkout has passed through.

q7.answer: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which checks the signature, records the event id, and applies a guarded update to the payment row. Each applied change writes an outbox row, and a relay publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to the broker. Order consumes the event and acts only while the order is AWAITING_PAYMENT.

q8.answer: Payment checks the signature first, then inserts the event id into webhook_events under a unique constraint, so a repeat, including a racing copy, is acknowledged and changes nothing. The guarded update also applies only when the payment is in the state the event expects, and a repeat that does not apply writes no outbox row.

q9.answer: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined through its outbox, and Order, while AWAITING_PAYMENT, sets FAILED_PAYMENT and makes one release call to Inventory, which changes the reservation from HELD to RELEASED and puts the stock back on sale. If the release gets no answer it is not retried, and the 10-minute sweeper frees the hold instead.

q10.answer: Order asks Inventory to claim the reservation. If the hold has lapsed, Inventory makes one attempt to re-reserve and claim the same lines in a single transaction: if the lines are still free the order is confirmed, and if not the claim is refused, Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and Payment refunds in full. Whether the business wants this retry rather than an immediate refund is listed under open questions.

q11.answer: Payment's refunds table holds a row, keyed on the order id, that starts as REFUND_PENDING before the provider is called. A failed refund is retried with backoff using the same key, and after the last attempt the row becomes REFUND_FAILED and an ops alert is raised, with the row staying open until someone resolves it. Whether ops should also retry automatically after the last attempt is still an open question.

q12.answer: Order's OrderConfirmed event, written to its outbox with the CONFIRMED status change, causes Cart's consumer to remove the ordered lines. It removes only the lines that still match the ordered quantity and price, so lines changed or added after Place order stay, and the consumer is idempotent on order id. Whether the business wants later edits kept rather than the whole cart emptied is still an open question.
